We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(x,z)}^{{u}_{2}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{3}(x,z)}^{{u}_{4}(x,z)}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type III region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,\,(x+1)^{3}\le z\le 2-{x}^{2},\,\,x+z\le y\le z+2}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $y,$ the $y$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{(x+1)^{3}}^{2-{x}^{2}}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{c}^{d}{\int }_{{v}_{3}(z)}^{{v}_{4}(z)}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $xz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/5f586edef4202e3f3de09fe947c955de62efa35e421e85b3e5034efd375790a7.png)

The region $D$ is a type I region in the $xz$-plane:

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,(x+1)^{3}\le z\le 2-{x}^{2}}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}y\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x$ to $\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z,$ we split $D$ into two type II regions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081417/assets/ec9845e347959ff1ac43a12d03261b1eb31172f14b56269d7bbfcb86a2a23e48.png)

Notice that the bottom and top boundaries of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(z),$ are

$\,$ $x=-1\,$ and $\,x=\sqrt[3]{z}-1.$

Also, the bottom and top boundaries of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(z),$ are

$\,$ $x=-\sqrt{2-z}\,$ and $\,x=0.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}={(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,-1\le x\le \sqrt[3]{z}-1}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}={(x,z)\,:\,1\le z\le 2,\,-\sqrt{2-z}\le x\le 0}.
$$

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{\sqrt[3]{z}-1}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{-\sqrt{2-z}}^{0}{\int }_{x+z}^{z+2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$
